Nik handed his horse to one of his men and turned to her.
Without a word, he swept her into his arms and kissed her.

‘What are you …’
‘They paid well.
They’ve their own food, and can make do in here for the night.
Then they’ll be on their way to the Mountains tomorrow.
Up there, no one cares what we do.
There’s no danger, Tel, you worry too much.’
‘I have to worry for two, for you haven’t the sense to.
I’ve food ready, but not enough for all this lot.
Why didn’t you send a bird to warn me?’
‘I did.
Didn’t it get here?
Maybe the storm delayed it.’
‘That’s what you always say when you don’t think to do it.’
‘Let it go, woman.
I’ve good tidings for you.
Let’s go back to your house and talk.’
Nik’s arm rested easily about her waist as they left.
It was up to his men to settle us.
There was straw to sleep in and plenty of space to spread it.
There was a dug well with a bucket outside for water.
There was a small hearth at one end of the barn.
The chimney smoked badly, but it sufficed to cook on.
The barn was not warm, save in comparison to the weather outside.
But no one complained.
Nighteyes had stayed outside.
They’ve a coop full of chickens, he told me.
And a pigeon coop, too.
Leave them alone, I warned him.
Starling started to leave with Nik’s men when they went up to the house, but they stopped her at the door.
‘Nik says all of you are to stay inside tonight, in one place.’
The man shot a meaningful glance at me.
In a louder voice, he called, ‘Get your water now, for we’ll be bolting the door when we leave.
It keeps the wind out better.’
No one was fooled by his comment, but no one challenged it.
Obviously the smuggler felt the less we knew of his bolthole, the better.
That was understandable.
Instead of complaining we fetched water.
Out of habit, I replenished the animals’ trough.
As I hauled the fifth bucket, I wondered if I would ever lose the reflex of seeing to the beasts first.
The pilgrims had devoted themselves to seeing to their own comfort.
Soon I could smell food cooking on the hearth.
Well, I had dried meat and hard bread.
It would suffice.
You could be hunting with me.
There’s game here.
They had a garden this summer and the rabbits are still coming for the stalks.
He sprawled in the lee of the chicken house, the bloody remnants of a rabbit across his forepaws.
Even as he ate, he kept one eye on the snow-covered garden patch, watching for other game.
I chewed a stick of dry meat glumly while I heaped up straw for Kettle’s bed in the stall next to her horse.
I was spreading her blanket over it when she returned from the fire carrying her teapot.
‘Who put you in charge of my bedding?’ she demanded.
As I took a breath to reply, she added, ‘Here’s tea if you’ve a cup to your name.
Mine’s in my bag on the cart.
There’s some cheese and dried apples there as well.
Fetch it for us, there’s a good lad.’
As I did so, I heard Starling’s voice and harp take up a tune.
Singing for her supper, I didn’t doubt.
Well, it was what minstrels did, and I doubted she’d go hungry.
I brought Kettle’s bag back to her, and she portioned me out a generous share while eating lightly herself.
We sat on our blankets and ate.

paragraphPairs.sourceText: ‘Let it go, woman. I’ve good tidings for you. Let’s go back to your house and talk.’ Nik’s arm rested easily about her waist as they left. It was up to his men to settle us. There was straw to sleep in and plenty of space to spread it. There was a dug well with a bucket outside for water. There was a small hearth at one end of the barn. The chimney smoked badly, but it sufficed to cook on. The barn was not warm, save in comparison to the weather outside. But no one complained. Nighteyes had stayed outside.
paragraphPairs.translatedText: — Облиш, жінко. Я маю для тебе добрі новини. Ходімо назад до твоєї хати й поговорімо. Нік невимушено обійняв її за талію, і вони пішли. Його людям довелося влаштовувати нас. Там була солома, щоб спати, й удосталь місця, щоб її розстелити. Надворі був викопаний колодязь із відром для води. В одному кінці хліва було невелике вогнище. Димар страшенно димів, але для готування годився. Хлів не був теплим, хіба що в порівнянні з погодою надворі. Та ніхто не скаржився. Нічноокий лишився надворі.

I brought Kettle’s bag back to her, and she portioned me out a generous share while eating lightly herself. We sat on our blankets and ate. During the meal, she kept glancing at me, and finally declared, ‘You’ve a familiar cast to your features, Tom. What part of Buck did you say you were from?’

targetSpanMissingExamples.sourceSentenceText: But a moment later, she pushed him away.

targetSpanMissingExamples.sourceSentenceText: Then they’ll be on their way to the Mountains tomorrow.
targetSpanMissingExamples.translatedParagraphText: — Вони добре заплатили. У них є власна їжа, і вони якось перебудуть тут ніч. А завтра рушать далі, до Гір. Там, нагорі, нікому немає діла до того, що ми робимо. Небезпеки немає, Тел, ти забагато тривожишся.

targetSpanMissingExamples.sourceSentenceText: Didn’t it get here?
targetSpanMissingExamples.translatedParagraphText: — Послав. Хіба він не прилетів? Може, буря його затримала.

targetSpanMissingExamples.sourceSentenceText: Nik’s arm rested easily about her waist as they left.
targetSpanMissingExamples.translatedParagraphText: — Облиш, жінко. Я маю для тебе добрі новини. Ходімо назад до твоєї хати й поговорімо. Нік невимушено обійняв її за талію, і вони пішли. targetSpanMissingExamples.sourceSentenceText: And a pigeon coop, too.
targetSpanMissingExamples.translatedParagraphText: У них курник, повний курей, сказав він мені. І голубник теж.

targetSpanMissingExamples.sourceSentenceText: Starling started to leave with Nik’s men when they went up to the house, but they stopped her at the door.
targetSpanMissingExamples.translatedParagraphText: Старлінг почала йти з людьми Ніка, коли вони рушили до будинку, але біля дверей її зупинили. — Нік каже, що всі ви маєте цієї ночі лишатися всередині, в одному місці. targetSpanMissingExamples.translatedParagraphText: Його слова нікого не обдурили, але ніхто їм не заперечив. Очевидно, контрабандист вважав: що менше ми знаємо про його схованку, то краще.
